podcast.title: Departure from Alexisonfire – Creative Differences and Focus on City and Colour
podcast.body: Dallas Green left Alexisonfire due to creative differences, seeking to devote himself fully to his solo project City and Colour. His departure was handled amicably and ultimately proved beneficial for all parties. "Left Alexisonfire due to creative differences, seeking to focus on City and Colour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Amicable Breakup and Solo Growth – "The Best Thing That Could Have Happened to All of Us"
xref.body: Dallas Green left the band to focus on City and Colour due to creative differences. The remaining members attempted to continue without him before acknowledging that the band without Green would not be Alexisonfire, leading to an amicable split. The separation allowed each member to grow independently; when they reunited, they did so on their own terms, prioritizing enjoyment and work-life balance over the demands of constant touring. "The separation allowed all the members to grow individually, and when they reunited, they did so on their own terms."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Dallas Green's Departure
xref.body: Dallas Green decided to leave the band not for solo success, but due to creative differences, feeling he could no longer write aggressive music and did not want to force it. He attempted to continue both Alexis on Fire and City and Colour but found he couldn't write aggressive material naturally anymore. The breakup was amicable, and it was acknowledged that he "probably should have left Alexis on Fire four years earlier" as City and Colour had begun to eclipse Alexis on Fire in popularity. "I left the band solely because I had creatively I wanted to do something else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Screamo Influence
xref.body: Sasha was one of the bands mentioned by Dallas Green as an influence for the early "screamo" sound that helped inform Alexis on Fire's distinct style, part of a collection of lesser-known acts that band members sought out in their youth. "I was kind of more the deep head early first-screamo stuff like where I was listening to bands like Sasha, Love Lost, Penoffa, Godden, these are all different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Screamo Influence
xref.body: Love Lost was cited by Dallas Green as an influence on the early "screamo" sound that shaped Alexis on Fire's music. This was part of a specific subgenre of aggressive music that required active searching to discover, often through vinyl distros at local shows. "I was kind of more the deep head early first-screamo stuff like where I was listening to bands like Sasha, Love Lost, Penoffa, Godden, these are all different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Eclipsing Alexis on Fire
xref.body: By the time Dallas Green left Alexis on Fire, his solo project, City and Colour, had grown significantly in popularity. It was noted that City and Colour had "eclipsed Alexis on Fire at that point," influencing Green's decision to leave the band to focus on his creative passion for different musical styles. "City and Colour had a clip to Alexis on fire at that point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

xref.title: Elk's Lodge Performance
xref.body: After meeting Liam from Vincent Black Shadow at a Converge show, George Pettit and Dallas Green later went to an Elk's Lodge to see Vincent Black Shadow perform, further illustrating the grassroots, community-driven nature of the music scene at the time. "And then we went to some like Elk's Lodge to go see Vincent Black Shadow play one time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Limited Influence on Alexis on Fire
xref.body: While a heavy band, The Melvins were explicitly mentioned as a band that none of the Alexis on Fire members, except potentially Dallas Green, were listening to as an influence, highlighting specific sonic preferences even within heavy music. "None of us were listening to the Melvents. Right. You were listening to the Melvents, right?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Meeting at a Converge Show
xref.body: George Pettit and Dallas Green met Liam from Cancer Bats (who was then in Vincent Black Shadow) while waiting in line to see a Converge show, highlighting the close-knit nature of the underground music scene where many of these artists connected. "George and I met, we met Liam from the Cancer Bats in line at a Converge show."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Members' Activities During Hiatus
xref.body: During the band's break, Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ and in other bands; Jordan Hastings played with Billy Talent; and Chris Steele undertook an expedition to the Himalayas. "Dallas Green focused on City and Colour; George Pettit became a firefighter; Wade McNeil worked as a radio DJ."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Opportunity Post-Breakup
xref.body: After Alexis on Fire's initial breakup, Wade McNeil joined The Gallows. This move was one of the individual paths taken by the band members when Alexis on Fire decided to halt operations due to Dallas Green's departure and the difficulty of writing new music without him. "He had the opportunity to join the gallows. So he went and did that and we all went our separate ways."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

xref.title: Post-Breakup Lives
xref.body: Following the band's breakup, members pursued different paths: Dallas Green continued with City and Colour, George Pettit became a firefighter, Wade McNeil became a radio DJ, Jordan Hastings became a fill-in drummer for Billy Talent and played in other bands, and Chris Steele was last heard to have gone for a "truck on the Himalayas." "I mean, Dallas Green is off doing a city and color thing. Vocalist George Pettit became a firefighter. Wade McNeil is doing a bunch of stuff, including working as a radio DJ. Drummer Jordan Hastings is filling it with Billy Talbot and playing in some other bands. And I'm not even sure where bass player Chris Steele is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

xref.title: Reunion Motivation
xref.body: The reunion was driven by the members remaining close, enjoying playing together, and sensing strong public demand. They initially played sporadic shows as a "vacation," but Dallas Green's move back to Toronto led to more regular practices and the decision to write new music, rather than just playing old hits. Despite the challenges of balancing music with family life and other aspirations, the "neural pathway" carved through years of playing live made returning feel natural and joyful. "It just became, it became no excuse for us to not play. Yeah. That's really what it was."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

xref.title: Shared Influence
xref.body: Converge was a band that all members of Alexis on Fire "kind of came together" on as an influence. George Pettit and Dallas Green even met Liam from Cancer Bats at a Converge show, indicating its significance in their formative musical experiences. "Converge, I think we all kind of came together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alexisonfire - In Their Own Words Podcast

xref.title: Touring Challenges
xref.body: The band experienced significant disparity in audience numbers during their early tours. For example, they played a successful show at the Croatian Cultural Center in Vancouver to a thousand people with Billy Talent, only to cross the border into Bellingham, Washington, and play for only the bar staff, with Dallas Green not even performing due to voice issues. Later, attempts to "hammer it" in America during the "Old Crows" era, including a "disastrous" Warped Tour and long unfulfilling American tours where only 40-60% of shows were good, became mentally exhausting. "We played for the bar staff. I don't even think I played the show. You didn't. I didn't. I took a T-shirt. Because your voice was bothering you."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Watch Out Album Artwork
xref.body: The artwork for the "Watch Out" album features two Catholic schoolgirls engaged in a knife fight. This imagery was inspired by a long-standing joke where the band would describe their sound on flyers as "two Catholic schoolgirls in a knife fight." Dallas Green photographed his then-girlfriend and her friend, who were actual Catholic high school students at the time and wore their own school uniforms for the shoot. "So when you make flyers for a show, back in the day you'd always have like the name of the band and then underneath it in parentheses or whatever, we'd have a little description of what the band was. And it was always something like, you know, crushing buffalo metal core or like, you know, whatever."
